text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Hannes Androsch, whose investment group plans to take over Austria's salt producer Salinen AG with Upper Austria's Raiffeisenlandesbank, says the salt company should become a market leader in Central Europe. Close cooperation with Dutch Frima would also be planned.
- Benetton is closing down its Austrian ski production plant Kaestle. Half the jobs are to be cut and the production machinery will be sold to other ski producers.
- Austria's tourism industry is in a state of alarm as German tourists and the media are criticising the country's motorway fees, the Vienna parking police and alleged viral infections.

- The U.S. dollar's strength is raising Austria's inflation rate. Economic research institute Wifo is becoming more sanguine on Austria's ailing export industry. Unemployment is also expected to fall, while the Maastricht criteria is expected to be reached more easily.
- Austria and the European Union are both sticking to their point of view regarding anonymous savings accounts.
- Motor engineer Steyr Fahrzeugtechnik is benefiting from development orders from car producers Daewoo and Audi.
- While Wifo expects a positive outcome from the European Monetary Union, Germans are growing more sceptical of the euro.
- Conservative union OeAAB boss Werner Fasslabend wants to use savings for new investments in a so-called "Austria-fund" to boost the country's economy.
- State secretary for financial affairs Peter Ruttensdorfer expects the euro to provide more employment. He also said there is no future for stocks from Eastern Europe on Vienna's stock exchange.
- The federal audit office has criticised as too risky Bank Austria's 250 million schilling credit to newspaper Der Standard.
